title: State of RPG Maker on Linux

posts.author: MushroomCake28
posts.body:
Hi all,
First off, it's been a while, I hope you all have been doing well. I stopped gamedev for a while (basically since the end of uni and starting to work), but thinking of coming back and finishing the project I had more or less stalled.
I've decided to move from Windows to Linux recently for many reasons (not gamedev related) and was just wondering if other people here are developing on Linux? If so, what's your experience? Should I stick to MV, or MZ through proton?
I've tinkered a bit for the past day (on Fedora 44), and it seems proton 9.0.4 with MZ gives an ok experience. MV on the other hand, which supposedly runs natively on linux, has been giving me some trouble with some lag and unresponsiveness. Both version suffer from same icon and UI in general (I'm on an ultrawide 3440x1440), but it's workable I suppose.
Thanks everyone!

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Hey Mush! Long time no see.
Over the past year I moved a lot of my development to a Framework 13 laptop running Pop_OS (which is an Ubuntu based distro)
I haven't tried running MZ via proton on this device since I primarily develop in MV. In that regard, I can report that, at least for my set up, MV in general runs the same if not smoother than my Win11 desktop.
If you recently switched to Linux (like myself) I actually recommend either Mint or Pop OS as they are geared towards beginners. That's not just in UI, but also the package manager and what drivers (and how it handles them) come with the distro.
I chose Pop_OS over Mint because while I not only appreciate, but highly respect community run and managed FOSS, there is concerns about the reliability of outsourcing lots of code to various people as well as how long the team might remain motivated. I'm sure with a little research these ideas might be put to rest, but rather than spend the time researching the team and the philosophy, I knew that System 76, developers of Pop OS, had a good reputation and are a company, therefore is likely more stable long-term comparatively.
I digress, either one is highly rated amongst the trend of Win11 refugees seeking better alternatives.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
I don't recall any sort of special set up. I pretty much just downloaded Steam, RPG Maker MV, clicked launch and was good to go.
I don't know how true this is, but I personally feel, more than Windows, performance on Linux is very hardware dependent. So it's worth noting my own hardware:
32GB RAM, Intel 1185G7, Intel Xe Graphics
Linux is pretty notorious for not handling dedicated GPU drivers well. This isn't entirely Linux's fault, but more the manufacturers who don't do much development for Linux.
AMD generally performs well with some hiccups, Nvidia doesn't give 2 cents about Linux and has the most problems (probably from the RTX30-series and up things got better, but if you are running 20-series or older you're gonna have a bad time), and Intel does well - but their drivers are pretty limited universally.
This is another reason why going with the "beginner friendly" distro like Mint or Pop_OS is best, because they come configured to handle
those
drivers better.
I simply bring this up since you mention performance. It almost makes me wonder if RM is trying to default to your GPU, but it's drivers aren't configured properly (because Linux).
As an aside, since we are talking about distros, there is one last one I want to mention for your consideration:
Bazzite.
Bazzite is different in a more intrinsic way than other Linux distros as it's primary focus is to be a gaming-centric distro that doesn't get in the way of the user. It is considered to be the absolute most beginner friendly, since it uses an immutable design, which, hell if I know exactly what that means on a technical level, but as far as the user is concerned, you can't brick your system because you accidentally apt before your sudo'd or whatever.
In addition to that, since it's primarily designed for gamers, they even have specific, community made configurations for GPU drivers, including graphics cards before the RTX 20 series.
I have actually used Bazzite some, as I have an older 1080ti system I put together from older parts. Overall, I definitely prefer Pop_OS, but I thought I should bring it up for your consideration anyways as another beginner friendly distro.
(It's worth reporting that many Unity engine games performed reasonably well with my 1080ti on Bazzite - I never tried anything more taxing though)

Hell yeah brother. We're the 10%!
I have a 9070XT in my desktop.
Since you mention LLMs, if you aren't opposed to using them, I've actually found they seem to be pretty good at troubleshooting Linux-specific problems.
For example, the package manager, Pop Shop, became unable to install updates, instead spitting out an error. Feeding that error into ChatGPT and explaining my problem it gave me a pretty quick command to run in the terminal to get things sorted.
It also helped me set up a network shared folder that Windows can see which has made life at home so much easier.
A few years back I ran Ubuntu - well before the AI era we are in now - and so I relied on the community to assist with problems and...it was pretty nasty and unforgiving. The Linux neckbeard reputation - at least back then - is based in reality, lol. So seemed easier to just ask a chatbot.
It - as is often the case - is not always right, or may produce a more roundabout solution to an easy problem, but for surface level issues, I think it's pretty effective tool for getting to grips with setting up Linux.
It probably wouldn't hurt to describe your specific RPG Maker problem to a chatbot and seeing if it can produce anything helpful towards troubleshooting it. Likely fixing whatever the underlying problem is is going to be a lot easier than having to configure a new OS installation.

I had the same issue for MV on Linux Mint, turns out it was caused by RPG Maker using an old version of nwjs that doesn't work well with Linux or something. Updating the nwjs that's included with RPG Maker seemed to fix this for me, perhaps it might be worth a try? (Of course, back up the old nwjs before attempting this, just in case)
